correctness.rationale: The full proof reduces intervention benefit to (1-q_i)s_i v_i, bounds weighted descendant counts by twice the (Delta-1)-ary growth, and constructs an explicit full (Delta-1)-ary subtree isolated from a unique maximum-in-degree decoy. The padded construction realizes matching orders at every sufficiently large n. Leaf peeling and positive-denominator cycle closure give an exact O(n) alternative. The actual packaged verifier independently compares 3413 successor configurations, 880 heterogeneous models, 880 brute-force k-subset choices, and 36 extremal-family instances.

originality.rationale: The targeted novel statement is the fixed-degree two-sided asymptotic loss hierarchy for an unambiguous in-degree intervention heuristic, not the previously known PageRank level-count formula or influence-based top-k rule. The inspected 2023, 2016, 2024 and 2026 works do not assert or imply both bounds and constructions. The 2005 related paper was read at abstract level only, leaving a stated priority risk.
residual_risks: Fortunato et al. (2005) directly investigate in-degree approximations to PageRank; complete primary text was not inspected, so a specialized overlapping worst-case theorem cannot be excluded.
Other PageRank/Katz centrality approximation results could imply the exact fixed-degree hierarchy under another terminology.
Full publisher-hosted rendering of Arratia and Marijuán (2016) was not retrievable directly; substantive theorem and section content was accessible through indexed HTML text.

value.rationale: The naturally motivated exact performance of an in-degree heuristic used in the 2023 motivating paper is classified at every fixed maximum in-degree: bounded, logarithmic or polynomial loss. The upper and lower bounds match, examples are connected and have uniform opinions and unique heuristic choices, and a linear-time exact functional-network alternative isolates failure of the proxy rather than intrinsic hardness. This is a complete structural asymptotic result, not a small numerical discrepancy.
